pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.t: casa
examples.r: KAH-sah

examples.t: mesa
examples.r: MEH-sah

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.t: hola
examples.r: OH-lah

examples.t: jueves
examples.r: HWEH-vehs

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.t: niño
examples.r: NEEN-yoh

examples.t: calle
examples.r: KAH-yeh

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.t: pero
examples.r: PEH-roh

examples.t: perro
examples.r: PEH-rroh

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.t: gracias
examples.r: GRAH-syahs

examples.t: café
examples.r: kah-FEH

alphabet.title: The Indonesian alphabet: 26 letters, five pure vowels
alphabet.explain: Indonesian uses the Latin alphabet exactly as it appears in English, with five vowels that are always pure (a e i o u) and no letter that changes its mind. If you can read it, you can say it.

letters.tip: schwa in the middle: baca = ba-ca

counting.title: Counting in Indonesian: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Learn 0-12 by heart. Thirteen and up is the number + belas: tiga belas, empat belas, lima belas.
rules: Stress falls on the second-to-last syllable: se-PU-luh.Every syllable is open (consonant + vowel), so words sound even and rhythmical.
The middle e is a short schwa: rumah = roo-mah, not roo-meh.
